key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes a taxonomy of safety and security failures for surgical robots as cyber-physical systems.
Danish law can adequately compensate patients after adversarial attacks, with no sharp safety/security distinction.
Patients can sue manufacturers directly under Danish product liability, via the Product Liability Directive, case law or contract.
Manufacturer liability can be removed by choosing a public-law compensation route.
EU Medical Device Regulation covers security and safety implicitly and adds substantial manufacturer duties and regulator powers.
annotation.summary_en: Legal analysis of liability when adversarial cyberattacks cause surgical robot failures. It builds a safety/security failure taxonomy and examines Danish national law and EU law, including the Medical Device Regulation. It concludes that Danish law adequately compensates patients and that EU law implicitly covers security while imposing heavy manufacturer duties.
annotation.title_clean: Dissecting liabilities in adversarial surgical robot failures: A national (Danish) and European law perspective
annotation.title_en: Dissecting liabilities in adversarial surgical robot failures: A national (Danish) and European law perspective
